cooccure: co-occurrence networks from many kinds of data

Source: R/cooccure-package.R
cooccure-package.Rd

cooccure builds co-occurrence networks, in which two items are linked when they appear in the same transaction: the keywords of one article, the genres of one film, the actors of one cast, or the states of one learning session. The network shows which items tend to go together and how a field, a corpus or a set of sessions is organized around them. The weight of a link starts as the number of shared transactions; because frequent items co-occur often by chance alone, it can be normalized for item frequency by one of eight similarity measures (van Eck & Waltman, 2009), and each transaction's contribution can be counted fractionally (Perianes-Rodriguez et al., 2016) or with a position decay. One network can be built per group (split_by) or one network pooled over groups (aggregate_by).

All of this is done by one function, cooccurrence(). It reads delimited columns, long (item, transaction) tables, binary and one-hot tables, wide sequences, lists of vectors and raw event logs, with sliding windows over ordered sequences and eight scalings of the weights, and returns the network as a tidy edge list.

Results

The edge list prints with a diagnostic header. summary.cooccurrence() computes network, node and group metrics; as.data.frame.cooccurrence() returns the edge, node and group tables; plot.cooccurrence() draws a heatmap, a network or the degree distribution.

Conversion

as_matrix() returns the weight or count matrix; as_igraph(), as_tidygraph(), as_cograph() and as_netobject() convert to the graph classes of igraph, tidygraph, cograph and Nestimate. The network is undirected except for similarity = "relative", which is directed.

Data

movies, actors and actor_genres are drawn from the IMDb non-commercial datasets; demo is a small hand-built cast table. launch_app() opens an interactive explorer.

References

van Eck, N. J., & Waltman, L. (2009). How to normalize cooccurrence data? An analysis of some well-known similarity measures. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 60(8), 1635–1651. doi:10.1002/asi.21075

Perianes-Rodriguez, A., Waltman, L., & van Eck, N. J. (2016). Constructing bibliometric networks: A comparison between full and fractional counting. Journal of Informetrics, 10(4), 1178–1195. doi:10.1016/j.joi.2016.10.006
